notes.title: Tower Defense Sale Update!
notes.content:
Hey all,

It's finally here, our first big update timed for our first discounted sale for Engineered to Purpose. Thank you for your patience - we hope you enjoy the changes that we're rolling out for the game. Here's a full breakdown of all of the changes:

Targeting Type Revamp
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/b384c65f0046df114f7355e229530c1d4dc98168.png
-Targeting type is set on tower placement rather than changed in real-time
-World 2 balance has been updated to account for this change

Minelayer
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/d8d54063c2627ba54d63701ba699d9a0be4d7346.gif
-New weapon component added to the game that fires mines that explode when enemies are within range

Saturation replaces Heuristics
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/59a5c9ddd05a4b37026fd05485b0c0ca9151ae37.gif
-Saturation modifier added to Blaster towers, giving them a charge of percentage-based damage every few seconds
-Heuristics modifiers on existing towers will be replaced with Power modifiers

Tower Charge visuals
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/0b1b9ba696233e04929350c94ee89ab92011c31d.gif
-Added clearer visualization for charging mechanics on towers when you select them
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/e9727b8b36c35911bad8a0cd20ff258e55ec0efe.gif
-Added special visual logic for laser ramp and saturation

SFX Pass
-Added new SFX for various UI elements and in-game interactions

Bug Fixes
-Fixed issues with updating towers
-Adjusted visuals for critical damage hit
-Fixed issues with convertor passive not triggering save
-Cursor can no longer leave the screen
-Can switch monitor that the game shows up on in settings now
-Fixed issues with the Accelerator convertor
-Some performance optimization

Thanks again everyone, cheers!
Engineered to Purpose Team

notes.title: Important Update: No Early Access
notes.content:
Hey everyone! 

While our intention was to release in Early Access, we have ended up going for full launch (its complicated), and so we need anyone buying the game to know: 

This game is a work in progress, NOT a finished game. We think that the current state of the game is polished enough that you should get a lot of value out of it - but there is a lot of planned content that is not in place yet, and we want you to be able to make an informed decision when buying the game.

As of launch, half of the game is basically done. The story campaign and levels are in place, and the mechanics are very playable. However two more worlds and the conclusion of our story, new components to build with, new enemy types, and new game modes for post-story replayablity are all coming soon!

We are committed as a dev team to completing this project with as much involvement of players as possible in the design. We'll be updating the Steam page as well to let those who are buying the game know what the current state of the game is.

We'll be looking to release a loose roadmap of our intended plan going forward soon. If you want to stay more directly in the loop with development please join our discord, we'd love to see you there:
https://discord.gg/NBWt438uJH


Apologies if this causes any issues for anyone - do let us know if so, happy to discuss with anyone who has any concerns.

Thanks again all!
Engineered to Purpose Team

notes.title: Development Log: #02
notes.content:
Development Log: #02 - Have a Blaster!

Hello hello hello - I'm returning with another development log covering some of the mechanics of Engineered to Purpose.

This time around I'm doing a deep dive into the first weapon you get in the game: 

The Blaster
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/6273d8e4d7a98b633b71fc99ca795bf7da4d57e5.gif
The Blaster is a big 'ol cannon that shoots big 'ol bullets. It costs less than all of the other weapons - which corresponds to it dealing less damage overall. It makes up for that in being a fast tower that can fire many shots - particularly when upgraded.

It starts off with Power and Tempo modifiers, which allow you to make the tower faster and deal more damage. 

At each tier you can get access to more modifier variants, starting with the pesky 
The Heuristics Modifier
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/fcec5ce4b32da52719f462aad8f087116174a7cd.gif
Heuristics adds damage for each time the tower kills an enemy. Towers with heuristics tend to start off weak, but when placed early they can scale up and become quite powerful with some upgrades (and difficult to balance q_q - hence the cap on the damage). 

At the Advanced tier we have:
The Replication Modifier
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/ed22ef9976315d1ca7b55543b7e24a16ab093c93.gif
Replication queues up multiple bullets to fire in a row before reloading. This adds a significant amount of damage - but also comes at a diminishing amount of damage per extra replication modifier. The more bullets you copy - the less damage the copy does. Originally it was just a straight up double of the damage, but we've been realizing that it's too strong and needed to come down a level or so in order to keep the pool of modifiers at a reasonable balance.

Next up at the Sophisticated tier there's:
The Bounce Modifier
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/88ccbfe311134b6f68a8ff74b536445a7e7b1b55.gif
This is a new modifier that we've been developing which makes it so that on impact the bullet will move to the next closest target in range, hit it and then move to the next closest target and so on, until it reaches a limit. Each bounce will do less and less damage - adding more modifiers
will improve the level of damage maintained between bounces. Originally we had a pierce modifier which caused bullets to move through enemies, but we typically found that it mostly passed through enemies without improving the overall damage. Bounce feels more in line with what we want to achieve.

Finally at the Transcendent tier:
The Stockpile Modifier
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/6abc0206f886ae1246440257785b1412703e549f.gif
We have our flashiest Blaster modifier here - it stockpiles projectiles around the tower in an orbit and then fires them repeatedly at targets when enemies are in range. Adding more of this modifier increases the number of projectiles you can stockpile and how fast they recuperate. You can unleash an absolute barrage of attacks using this modifier.

Thanks for checking out our development log for Engineered to Purpose. Just as a reminder, if you're interested in trying out the game, please give it a wishlist! We're also looking to start up a closed beta playtest this month. If you want to be a part of that, shoot us an e-mail at confidence.roll.games@gmail.com.

notes.title: Development Log: #01
notes.content:
Development Log: #01 - Here there be Components

Hello to the vastness of space that is the Steamosphere! We're a small development team called Confidence Roll Games working on a game called Engineered to Purpose. My name's Keely and I'm the team's "Something". As in, I do not really know what my role is at this point, I'm just kind of doing everything everywhere all at once with an almost borderline respectable level of competence.

As we're ramping up to releasing the game (and potentially beyond!) I'll be periodically releasing development logs talking about an assortment of things related to the game. If we have cool progress to show then we'll definitely include that, but I figured that it would be best to start off with some posts going over some of the mechanics of the game.

In which case, there's no better place to start than with..
THE COMPONENTS SYSTEM

Components are the building blocks that make up the towers. They're the bits that give the tower their identity and determine what purpose they will serve overall.

Weapons
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/cd39eccdc0723fc447967d62cd9bf13a5c2aabdc.gif
Weapons are used to establish what kind of attacks the tower will fire. Do you want them to hone in on targets? Instantly impact and deal ramping damage? Bombard enemies with an area of effect attack? Choosing a weapon is often the first step you'll take in determining what kind of tower you're making.

Generators
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/e30bf08016d1be820cf81ea7da2b603bdfc6bd60.gif
Generators give the tower its energy to power its attacks. The more powerful the generator, the more attacks you can add to a single tower!

Detectors
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/8dea1aacc575f54ccf761717fb3974792ff2c453.gif
Detectors provide towers their ability to target enemies. More powerful detectors will have more elaborate targeting schemes - like targeting specific types of enemies and prioritizing faster or stronger enemies.

Convertors
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43151476/3b37345a40133d75b2ae0eedc8745f433644301b.gif
Lastly we have the convertors. They're an optional component that's used to change the overall flavour of the tower. Want your tower to apply slow to enemies? The disruption convertor will make them chill out. Want your tower to do damage over time? The corruption convertor will shred enemies to bits long after they've left your target's range. The possibilities can get quite nutty when you start using convertors!

We'll leave off here for now! Thanks for reading our development log for Engineered to Purpose. If you're interested in trying out the game, please give it a wishlist! We're also looking to start up a closed beta playtest this month. If you want to be a part of that, shoot us an e-mail at confidence.roll.games@gmail.com.
